Hypothesis provider of a fitted model

Source: R/hypothesis-model-provider.R
hypothesis_provider.Rd

hypothesis_provider() is the single hook through which hypothesis_BF_model() reaches a model. Its method returns a provider, a list of the callbacks and values that the engine needs for the statements it plans: the parameter catalog and its entries, the draws of the tested quantities, the random-effect quantities, and the density backends that can evaluate them. The method for a BayesTools_fit returns the default provider, which implements every callback with the functions of BayesTools (parameter_catalog(), as_mixed_posteriors(), marginal_posterior(), parameter_mixed_posterior(), JAGS_formula_coefficient_transform(), and JAGS_formula_prior_density()). A downstream model class that wraps a fit starts from hypothesis_provider(<its fit>) and replaces the callbacks that differ with utils::modifyList(), so that it overrides only what is specific to its model.

hypothesis_provider(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
hypothesis_provider(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'BayesTools_fit'
hypothesis_provider(object, ...)

Arguments

object

a model object.

...

further arguments for methods.

Value

A provider, a list of class BayesTools_hypothesis_provider.

Details

A provider is a list of class BayesTools_hypothesis_provider; the engine checks it before use. Its elements are the following. The callbacks close over the model object.

kind

"model" (default) or "marginal_means".

object

the model object. It is hashed for the cache of plans and passed to the density backends.

fit

its BayesTools_fit, from which the transforms of formula coefficients and their prior densities are read.

capability_object

the object the density backends receive in available() and in their requests (default object).

build, refit_class

the name of the build in the requests to refit a model with outdated metadata ("Refit the model with the current <build> build."), and classes that precede BayesTools_refit_required in those conditions.

caller, random_point_mass_advice, transform_scaled_default

the name of the entry point in the reasons of refusals (default "hypothesis_BF()"); the sentence that ends the reason of a refused point null at a prior point mass of a random-effect quantity; and the scale of hypothesis_quantities() when transform_scaled is NULL.

ordinate_label

how the messages of refusals name the ordinate backends (default "ordinate density methods").

component_argument

the name of the argument through which the caller selects a value of components (default "namespace", the argument of hypothesis_BF_model() and of the method of hypothesis_BF() for a BayesTools_fit). The messages of the engine that name that argument ("The 'hypothesis' argument selects namespace = 'mu' but 'namespace' was set to 'random'.") use it; a model class that passes the selection under another name sets it, for example "component".

density_methods

the names that density_method can match, in order (default: the registered backends that are not of type "stored").

components

the selection vocabulary of the namespace argument as data: values (the accepted values, in the order of the error message), synonyms (a named character vector, for example c(location = "mods")), default ("auto"), refused (a named character vector of the reasons for which a component cannot be tested), random (the value that selects the random-effect quantities), and advice (the sentence that follows the message of an ambiguous statement).

metadata()

a list with the catalog (a parameter_catalog(), possibly extended with parameter_catalog_extend(); the engine parses and resolves with it) and the entries: a data frame with one row per tested parameter and the columns quantity_id, parameter (the name of the tested parameter), component (a value of components$values), term, source, formula_parameter, role ("formula_coefficient_group" for a whole factor term, whose levels are its member_quantity_ids), quantity, status, fixed_value, aliases (a list column), and member_quantity_ids (a list column). The alias rows of the catalog of the entries carry the component as their namespace and component.

uncovered(resolution, quantity_ids, symbol, metadata)

the refusal for resolved quantities that no entry covers: a list with reason and either type ("target" or "statement") or the complete condition class.

sample_parameters(parameter), mixed_posteriors(parameters, conditional, conditional_rule, transform_scaled, n_prior_samples), density_parameter(samples, parameter, sample_parameters), formula_name_map(formula_parameter)

the draws of a fixed coefficient: the prior-list names whose draws are mixed (the parameter and the owners of the fitted coordinates that its prior density combines), the mixed posteriors (as_mixed_posteriors()), the element of the samples that is the tested parameter, and the map of the formula coefficients to the fitted names.

random

the callbacks for the random-effect quantities: select(parameter, transform_scaled) (a list with the element spec, a list with the label and status of the quantity, and any elements the other callbacks need), mixed_posterior(parameter, transform_scaled, conditional, selected) (the mixed posterior as the one-element list returned by as_mixed_posteriors()), support(selected) (the exact bounds on the scale requested from select(), which are those of the draws), density_target(parameter, transform_scaled, operation) (a list with the quantity that a density backend evaluates, its parameter_spec, and display_transform, or the refusal of a quantity without one: its reason, and optionally its type ("target", the default, "method", or "fixed": the engine's refusal BayesTools_hypothesis_<type> and its parent BayesTools_hypothesis_unavailable) and its cause ("random_target", the default, or "original_scale"), for which the density backend appends its classes (refusal_classes(cause))), sd_pair(selected) (the standard deviation of which a variance is the square, or NULL), zero_boundary(selected) (NULL, or a list with the statement that tests the omission of a component), defined_share(values, selected, conditional), defined_footnote(label, samples, posterior_defined, prior_defined), defined_draws(values, samples, label) (the treatment of the draws at which a quantity is undefined), and prior_draws(parameter, selected, transform_scaled, n_samples, seed) (prior draws of a quantity without a prior density with provenance).

point_mass_reason()

NULL, or the text that replaces the reason of a point hypothesis at a prior point mass.

full_ensemble(parameter)

whether omitting conditional tests the parameter within the full ensemble, including the models in which it is fixed by its null component (the engine then warns); combination_hint(plan): NULL, or text appended to the refusal of a linear combination of the levels of such a term.

check_plans(plans)

NULL, or a function that validates the plans of all statements of a request and stops with a refusal.

check_density_control(density_method, density_control)

NULL, or a function that checks the density_control of a call before the control() of the density backend sees it. It receives the name of the selected backend and the settings as supplied (a list, possibly empty, or NULL) wherever control() is called: on every call with an ordinate backend, and on every call that supplies settings to another backend (for stored marginal means also where the stored settings are normalized). It stops with the condition that refuses the settings; its value is ignored. Without it the built-in backends accept NULL and an empty list and refuse other settings with the message 'density_control' is not used by density_method = 'KDE'., and the control() of a backend validates its own settings.

A provider of kind = "marginal_means" describes the stored marginal means of a model instead: inference (the marginal inference with the elements averaged and conditional), model_averaged (logical; model-averaged point statements are tested on the conditional draws and cannot mix with region statements), capability_object (the fit that the backends compute ordinates from, or NULL), select(hypothesis, parameter) (the marginal-means parameter and its aliases that a statement names), density_method_default() and density_control_default(density_method) (used when the arguments are NULL), and metadata() for hypothesis_quantities().

See also
